column3: NKJV has “came to Jesus,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “came to Him.”
NKJV has “born again,” where the Greek ἄνωθεν means “from above” or “again.” “Amen, amen” is rendered “Most assuredly.”
Close to the Greek; “from above” is rendered “again” (see verse 3).
NKJV includes “who is in heaven,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “the Son of Man.”
NKJV includes “should not perish but,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “that whoever believes may have eternal life in Him.”
Close to the Greek; “judge” is rendered “condemn.”
Close to the Greek; “judged” is rendered “condemned.”
Close to the Greek; “judgment” is rendered “condemnation.”
NKJV has “the Jews,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “a Jew.”
